facts.text: curvequery is a layer on PyVISA and the Visadore plugin manager for downloading waveform data from an oscilloscope
The curve feature is registered for the MSO44, MSO46, MSO54, MSO56 and MSO58 with the entry point curve = curvequery._tek_series_mso_curve_feat:TekSeriesCurveFeat
The package pins visadore 1.0, pyvisa 1.11.3 and tqdm 4.62.2 or later
TekSeriesCurveFeat.feature returns a WaveformCollection whose data maps each source name to a Waveform(data, x_scale, y_scale)
The source list comes from data:source:available? and only sources whose display:global:<source>:state reply is on are kept
A source is kept only when display:global:<source>:state? replies with a non-zero integer
The horizontal scale is slope = WFMOutpre:XINCR and offset = -PT_OFF * slope + XZERO, in the WFMOutpre:XUNIT unit
The analog vertical window is scale * (5 - position) to scale * (-5 - position), from the source's SCALE and POSITION queries
Analog samples are converted with WFMOutpre:YMUlt and WFMOutpre:YZEro
A decomposed digital bit is named <source>_D<bit> and each sample is (sample >> (2 * bit)) & 1
With decompose_dch the feature yields the eight bit channels; without it the same source becomes one 8-bit word
Each download takes its record length from horizontal:recordlength?
The record is read from data:start 1 to data:stop <record length>
The feature saves ACQuire:STATE and writes ACQuire:STATE STOP for the transfer
The feature restores the saved ACQuire:STATE after the transfer
Waveform is a namedtuple of data, x_scale and y_scale
WaveformCollection.sources returns the keys of data

safe_state.description: acquisition stopped during the transfer; the saved ACQuire:STATE is restored afterwards
